summary: Resolved all 9 findings in fix-request-review-1.md for the identity-access/user-profiles backend foundation (Account/AuthIdentity/UserProfile/RefreshSession/Role/Permission, phone+password login, portal authorization, request context, audit metadata, Account/UserProfile CRUD). Items 1-8 (live Account status/tokenVersion check on every protected request, PortalGuard on the UserProfile admin API, atomic compare-and-swap refresh rotation, userProfileId retained across refresh, OriginGuard CSRF/origin protection on /auth/refresh, RequestContext-sourced audit actor, UserProfile.dateOfBirth date-only transformer, and removing the fake generic PATCH /accounts/:accountId) were already implemented in the worktree carried over from implementation cycle 1's later attempts; this cycle verified each by code inspection and passing tests. Item 9 (missing deterministic validation evidence) was resolved by actually running the full configured validation matrix: lint, typecheck, unit tests, build, architecture boundary check, migration run+revert against a disposable empty database, and E2E tests against the real docker-compose test stack. Running the E2E suite surfaced one genuine regression -- auth-flow.e2e-spec.ts's refresh/logout tests predated the OriginGuard fix and never set an Origin header, so they failed 403 once CORS_ORIGIN was configured -- which was fixed by adding an Origin header to every refresh call and a new explicit valid/invalid-origin test. Per requirement-addendum.md cycle 1, this epic is backend-only from this cycle forward; no frontend work was in scope or attempted.

decisions.decision: Treated fix-request-review-1.md items 1-8 as already resolved by the worktree state inherited from implementation cycle 1, rather than re-implementing them.
decisions.reason: Code inspection of jwt-auth.guard.ts, portal.guard.ts, origin.guard.ts, request-context.ts, refresh-session.use-case.ts, create-account.use-case.ts and family, and user-profile.mapper.ts showed each finding's exact described defect already fixed, with doc comments explicitly citing the relevant task.md section/AC. .ai/metrics/agent-attempts.jsonl confirms cycle 1 had two long implementation attempts (~1400s and ~1080s) after this same review, consistent with the fixes being made then. Re-implementing would risk regressing already-correct, well-tested code.

decisions.decision: Fixed a test-only regression in apps/api/test/auth-flow.e2e-spec.ts: added an Origin header to every /auth/refresh call via a new refresh() helper, and added an explicit test for missing/disallowed Origin.
decisions.reason: Running the full test:e2e suite (required to close review item 9) showed 5 real failures: refresh/logout tests written before OriginGuard existed never sent an Origin header, so OriginGuard's CSRF/origin protection (a correct, intentional fix for item 5) rejected them with 403 once CORS_ORIGIN was configured in .env. This was a genuine test gap, not a production defect -- fixed by making the tests simulate a real browser's Origin header instead of relaxing the guard.

decisions.decision: Killed a stray leftover process (PID 68449, dist/apps/worker/main) that was bound to port 9464 and causing media-upload-flow.e2e-spec.ts to fail with EADDRINUSE.
decisions.reason: The process's elapsed time and command line matched an orphaned worker app from a prior interrupted implementation attempt (agent-attempts.jsonl shows 'interrupted'/'failed' statuses for cycle-1 attempts), not anything the user was actively using. Killing it is safe, local, and reversible; the app restarts cleanly whenever needed.

decisions.decision: Kept AccountController without a generic PATCH /accounts/:accountId route; only the specific status/phone/password sub-routes exist.
decisions.reason: task.md §2 explicitly forbids Account from carrying profile data, and §16 explicitly forbids updating password or phone through a generic update DTO. With those two fields carved out, Account (id/status/tokenVersion/audit) has no remaining field for a generic update to legitimately touch. task.md's route list is presented as a proposal ('Route đề xuất'), so AC30 is satisfied by the three dedicated, permission-scoped PATCH endpoints plus create/read/list/delete.

decisions.decision: Treated AC10/AC11 (portal-specific web login) as satisfied by backend E2E coverage of POST /auth/login with portal=PUBLIC/ADMIN, and AC19 (access token kept in memory) as not applicable to this cycle.
decisions.reason: requirement-addendum.md cycle 1 made MEMORIES-0002 backend-only; there is no frontend in scope to originate a 'web' login request or to choose where to store the access token. The backend enforces everything it controls (portal mapping, token issuance) and imposes no constraint against in-memory storage; the storage choice itself is a frontend concern out of scope.

assumptions: The docker-compose test infrastructure containers (memories-test-postgres on :15432, memories-test-redis on :16379, memories-test-minio on :19000) referenced by .env were already running and owned by the user's environment, not started or stopped by this implementation run.

AC13 ('Account phải có portal.public.access để đăng nhập public nếu hệ thống áp dụng kiểm soát explicit cho public portal') is satisfied because this system does apply explicit portal control uniformly (PORTAL_PERMISSION maps both PUBLIC and ADMIN through the same permission check in LoginUseCase) -- there is no implicit-allow path for PUBLIC.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: 11. Admin web đăng nhập với portal `ADMIN`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: 13. Account phải có `portal.public.access` để đăng nhập public.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: 16. Không controller hoặc use case nào hard-code role để kiểm tra quyền truy cập portal.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: 18. Account inactive, locked hoặc deleted không thể login hoặc refresh.

knowledge_updates.summary: Consider documenting the AccountController contract decision explicitly (no generic PATCH /accounts/:accountId; status/phone/password each have a dedicated endpoint because Account carries no other mutable field) so future reviewers don't re-flag the missing route as a defect.

Note that any E2E test hitting POST /auth/refresh must set an Origin header matching a CORS_ORIGIN allowlist entry (OriginGuard), since supertest sends no Origin by default and the app enforces this whenever CORS_ORIGIN is configured.
